subject: modify lm or loess function to use it within ggplot2’s geom_smooth

messages.author: 4c8481384f2d3218
messages.subject: modify lm or loess function to use it within ggplot2’s geom_smooth
parts:
I need to modify the lm (or eventually loess) function so I can use it
in ggplot2's geom_smooth (or stat_smooth).

For example, this is how stat_smooth is used normally:

> qplot(data=diamonds, carat, price, facets=~clarity) +
stat_smooth(method='lm')`

I would like to define a custom 'lm2' function to use as value for the
'method' parameter in stat_smooth, so I can customize its behaviour.

> lm2 <- function(formula, data, subset, ...)
{
print(head(data)) # example of lm's customization
return(lm(formula, data, subset, ...))
}
> qplot(data=diamonds, carat, price, facets=~clarity) +
stat_smooth(method='lm2')

Note that I have used method='lm2' as parameter in stat_smooth.
When I execute this code a get the error:

'Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : 'nthcdr' needs a list to CDR down'

Which I don't understand very well. The lm2 method works very well
when run outside of stat_smooth. I played with this a bit and I have
got different types of error, but since I am not comfortable with R'
debug tools it is difficult for me to debug them. The problem is that
I don't understand very well which output stat_smooth expects from lm
when it calls it and what I should put inside the return() call.


note: I have cross-posted this question on stackoverflow:
- http://stackoverflow.com/questions/2370648/derivate-lm-or-loess-function-to-use-it-within-ggplot2s-geom-smooth

--

On Fri, Mar 5, 2010 at 12:18 AM, hadley wickham <h.wi...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Well, in that case, the easiest thing is to wait until I fix that bug.
> Hadley

For the moment, I came out with an orrible hack in which I modified
loess to return some fake results, which are then plotted in an area
of the plot that I hide with setting x/y limits.

Here it is the code in case somebody has the same problem and he is in
a hurry for a fix:

loess2 <- function(formula, data, subset, ...){
x <- match.call()
x[[1]] <- quote(loess)

if (length(data$x) > 5)
{
eval.parent(x)
}
else
{
fakelm <-lm(-1:-length(x) ~ rep(-1, length(x)));
return(fakelm)
}
}

I wasn't able to understand what I could possibly pass to geom_smooth
with the return() call. I have tried with an empty dataset, but it
returned an error... maybe an empty dataset with $x and $y defined as
NAs, but now I am tired and I am happy with this temporary hack.

thanks also to who answered me on stackoverflow:
- http://stackoverflow.com/questions/2370648/modify-lm-or-loess-function-to-use-it-within-ggplot2s-geom-smooth
